text:
North Star Investment Management Corp. lowered its position in shares of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 2.6% in the 3rd quarter, HoldingsChannel reports. The fund owned 97,679 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 2,602 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 2.5% of North Star Investment Management Corp.’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 3rd largest position. North Star Investment Management Corp.’s holdings in Apple were worth $22,050,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other institutional investors and hedge funds have also recently made changes to their positions in the stock. Baxter Bros Inc. increased its position in shares of Apple by 6.2% during the third quarter. Baxter Bros Inc. now owns 7,984 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $1,802,000 after acquiring an additional 467 shares in the last quarter. Wall Street Access Asset Management LLC grew its position in Apple by 1.3% in the 3rd quarter. Wall Street Access Asset Management LLC now owns 22,967 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,183,000 after purchasing an additional 297 shares during the period. Vigilant Capital Management LLC grew its position in Apple by 3.0% in the 3rd quarter. Vigilant Capital Management LLC now owns 126,819 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $28,628,000 after purchasing an additional 3,693 shares during the period. Hudson Capital Management LLC grew its position in Apple by 1.7% in the 3rd quarter. Hudson Capital Management LLC now owns 20,903 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $4,719,000 after purchasing an additional 350 shares during the period. Finally, Kiley Juergens Wealth Management LLC grew its position in Apple by 12.9% in the 3rd quarter. Kiley Juergens Wealth Management LLC now owns 44,036 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,940,000 after purchasing an additional 5,035 shares during the period. 57.08% of the stock is owned by institutional investors.
Get Apple alerts: A number of equities research analysts have commented on the stock. Royal Bank of Canada set a $185.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Thursday. UBS Group set a $180.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Thursday. Goldman Sachs Group set a $140.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research report on Thursday. BidaskClub downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Tuesday, November 13th. Finally, ValuEngine downgraded shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Wednesday, November 21st. Three investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-three have issued a hold rating and twenty-three have issued a buy rating to the company. Apple presently has an average rating of “Hold” and an average target price of $210.72.
In other Apple news, SVP Angela J. Ahrendts sold 14,194 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction on Friday, October 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $227.96, for a total value of $3,235,664.24. Following the sale, the senior vice president now owns 105,538 shares in the company, valued at approximately $24,058,442.48. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through the SEC website . Also, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction on Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total transaction of $647,520.00. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now owns 8,940 shares in the company, valued at approximately $1,698,600. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . 0.06% of the stock is currently owned by insiders.
AAPL opened at $157.92 on Thursday. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87, a quick ratio of 1.09 and a current ratio of 1.12. Apple Inc. has a fifty-two week low of $146.59 and a fifty-two week high of $233.47. The firm has a market cap of $775.31 billion, a P/E ratio of 13.29, a PEG ratio of 1.21 and a beta of 1.23.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its earnings results on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 earnings per share for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.78 by $0.13. Apple had a net margin of 22.41% and a return on equity of 48.68%. The company had revenue of $62.90 billion for the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $61.55 billion. During the same quarter in the previous year, the company earned $2.07 EPS. Apple’s revenue for the quarter was up 19.6% on a year-over-year basis. As a group, equities analysts expect that Apple Inc. will post 13.18 earnings per share for the current year.

About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
